messages.text: I’ll research the opening route and battle systems, set up the gameplay archive, then start a separate save with only `HARDCAP`. I’ll keep notes and play until the first Gym Leader is defeated.

Julia uses Electric Terrain and a full team of six. I’m planning around Mudkip’s evolution into Marshtomp, plus early support Pokémon; the initial level cap is 20. I’ve also found the longer walkthrough and postgame route for future sessions. [Opening guide](https://bigjra.github.io/reborn/), [Gym strategy](https://reborn.sailor.li/walkthroughs/01_badge1).

I’m checking the recording before making any game progress.

The recording works and is cropped to the game window. Reborn’s title animation is running, but it hasn’t responded to the desktop tool’s keypresses yet. I’m checking that input issue before creating the save.

Reborn receives menu shortcuts, but its gameplay input polling misses the desktop tool’s instant key taps. May I use a local keyboard helper that holds keys briefly (for example via macOS CGEvent) to control the game? The computer-use tool’s rules require your explicit authorization to use another input method.
- Yes, use a local keyboard helper
- Keep trying the desktop tool only
The keyboard helper works. This is Reborn 19.5.43, and the menu is ready for a new save. I’ll name our trainer **Aster** and use only `hardcap`.
Aster’s new game has started. I’m proceeding through the train introduction to the password prompt, then heading for starter selection.
`hardcap` is confirmed enabled, and I declined further passwords. The recording is running; the input log will let me remove pauses spent planning or inspecting screens from the final 4× archive.
We’ve arrived in Reborn City. I’m heading east to the Grand Hall; after the starter battles, I’ll collect the early team members needed for Fern and Julia.
Mudkip is ours. Its Ground typing after evolution should be especially useful against Julia; I’ll add a second attacker before facing Fern’s Grass types.
Cain is defeated, and Mudkip reached level 6. The separate save is `Game_3.rxdata`, so the existing runs are intact. Victoria is next, followed by team building around Peridot Ward.
Victoria is defeated too; Mudkip is level 7. I’m collecting the Pokédex and Poké Balls, then going after Kricketot and a few useful wild encounters.
The introductory battles and registration are complete. I’m moving into Peridot Ward to recruit Kricketot, then I’ll train it alongside Mudkip and collect supplies before the factory sequence.
Kricketot has joined the team. I’m checking its ability and moves, then training it toward Kricketune so we have an answer to Fern’s Grass-heavy team.
Kricketot has Shed Skin, so I’ll use the early Ability Capsule to give Kricketune Technician after it evolves. For now, it will gain experience by starting battles and switching to Mudkip.
The level-10 Wimpod is too strong for this team yet, and its Special Attack reductions are blunting Water Gun. I’ll build up on the lower-level plaza battles before returning to this alley.
We’re back at the plaza’s beginner trainers. Kricketot’s Bide can handle these lighter hits, and a few levels will unlock its direct Bug attack.

The early training is slower than expected because Kricketot starts with only Growl and Bide. I’m switching to safer experience gains and catching additional Pokémon before attempting stronger trainers again.
Both Pokémon are healed. I’m expanding the team in the grass beside the Grand Hall, then returning to trainer battles with more options.
Rattata is caught, giving us a third Pokémon. I’m looking for a few more useful encounters here while Kricketot gains capture experience.
Bidoof is caught, and it has Moody—a useful ability for longer battles. I also tightened the input timing so each action finishes before I inspect the next screen.

That helps. I’ll build reusable movement routes and a screen-reading battle loop for routine training, and use turbo for repeated battles. I’ll still inspect captures, move learning, and major fights individually.

I’m adding screen recognition and reusable action sequences so routine battles and travel take fewer round trips. Bidoof has joined the team; I’ll save this progress and finish the first recording segment before continuing training.

The first archive is complete: about 50 minutes of recording became 4½ minutes at 4× after removing idle gaps. The next segment is recording now. I’m building Kricketot toward its first attacking move and Mudkip toward Marshtomp for Julia.
I found why turbo had little effect: frame skipping was disabled, which limits its speed. That is now enabled. I’m also tightening the key timing so repeated menu presses aren’t missed.

Kricketot has reached level 6 and learned Struggle Bug, so it can now train without relying on Bide. The battle helper is handling repeated attacks and level-up screens, with stops for unfamiliar choices.

The saved map routes are working now, including obstacle checks. That should make healing trips and city travel much more reliable. Next I’ll build enough strength to clear the early trainers and the factory sequence.

The early trainer battles are giving better experience than the grass, so I’m moving through those now. Kricketot is level 7. I’ll use the nearby healing station and trainer rewards to prepare for Fern before entering the factory.

Kricketot reached level 9 using the first trainer reward candy. It has beaten Claudette’s first Meowth and is fighting her second; evolution at level 10 will give it the stronger moves needed for the next stretch.

Kricketot evolved into Kricketune and learned Fury Cutter. I’ve healed the team and bought Potions, Antidotes, and more Poké Balls. I’m heading into Peridot to collect its Ability Capsule and continue toward Fern.

Fury Cutter is clearing the nearby trainers well. One Igglybuff slowed us down with sleep and infatuation, so I switched to Mudkip for the next opponent. The route helper now pauses automatically when a trainer interrupts travel.
Kricketune now has Technician, which boosts its weaker attacks and makes the opening Fury Cutter much stronger. The capsule is safely collected before the factory event can remove access to it.

Kricketune is level 12 and has cleared another two-Pokémon trainer. I’ve linked the route and battle helpers so they can handle routine encounters along the way, stopping for low health, new moves, or unfamiliar decisions.

Salandit exposed a weakness in the automatic battle choices: it knocked out Kricketune before I switched. Mudkip won with Water Gun and reached level 10. I’ve added a stop for dangerous type matchups and am healing before continuing.
We’ve reached Fern with the team healed. I’m pausing here to finish the next hourly archive, then I’ll resume with his battle and the factory.

The second archive is saved and verified: 58 minutes became 7¼ minutes at 4× after trimming idle time. Recording has restarted. Fern’s team is vulnerable to a built-up Fury Cutter, so I’ll try to keep Kricketune’s attack chain going through the fight.
Fern’s Rowlet is hitting hard, and paralysis has disrupted Kricketune’s attack chain. I’m adjusting the battle plan; the recording is still running.

I found and fixed a control-script issue: the move cursor changes color with the selected move, so it sometimes chose Growl instead of Fury Cutter. I reloaded the pre-battle save and am retrying with the corrected selector.
Fern is defeated. Kricketune reached level 15, and I’m heading to Mosswater Factory next. Fern’s healing between factory battles should help train Mudkip toward its Ground-type evolution for Julia.
The factory route is mapped, and the team is ready for the next story section. The first two trimmed, 4× recordings are verified and saved; the third recording is active.
Mudkip is now leading so it can gain experience in the factory’s double battles. I’m also tightening the menu timings so queued actions finish their transitions before the next input.
The first factory pair is beaten, and Mudkip gained two levels. Fern heals the team after these battles, so this is a useful stretch for building it up before the gym.
The factory’s first code terminal is activated. I’m working through the next guards with Water Gun while Fern supplies support; Mudkip is level 12 now.
Two factory battles are down, with Mudkip at level 13. I’ve also added a visual check to the pathing script so patterns on factory machinery aren’t mistaken for dialogue.
The factory field made Alolan Geodude’s Spark strong enough to knock out Mudkip. Kricketune is finishing this fight with Absorb; Fern will restore the team afterward.
Three factory pairs are beaten, and the next fight is underway. Kricketune is level 16; Mudkip still needs three levels to evolve, which should make Julia’s Electric attacks much easier to handle.
The elevator code is solved, and I’ve reached the second floor. Next are the explosives and the final factory battle, followed by preparation for Julia.
The second-floor guards are underway. Mudkip is level 14, and both main Pokémon are getting steady experience without needing trips back to the Pokémon Center.
Mudkip is level 15—one level from evolving. The second code’s last digit is collected, and I’m moving through the remaining factory rooms.
The next pair used Disable on Water Gun, so I’ve switched Mudkip to Tackle for the finish. The factory’s partner healing is keeping the team ready between fights.
Mudkip evolved into Marshtomp and learned Mud Shot. That gives us Electric immunity and a reliable Ground attack—the key pieces of the Julia plan.
Marshtomp is handling the remaining guards. After the factory boss, I’ll check levels and supplies before taking on Julia; I’ll stop as soon as her badge is secured.
All four digits for the explosives-room code are collected, and I picked up a hidden Super Potion for the upcoming boss fights.
I’m fighting the guards holding the explosives. Marshtomp’s Water Gun is well suited to their Solrock and Lunatone; the final factory pair is next.
The explosives are secured, and Marshtomp is level 18. I’m returning to Julia and Florinia to open the final factory room.
The final factory fight is underway against Aster and Eclipse. Marshtomp can ignore Thunder Fang and hit their Rockruff super effectively with Mud Shot.
Aster and Eclipse are defeated, and Marshtomp is level 19. I’m finishing the factory exit scene, then pausing to trim and save the hour’s recording at 4× before continuing to Julia.
The third archive is verified: 64 minutes became 8 minutes 39 seconds at 4× after idle trimming. I’m restarting recording and heading to the gym with Marshtomp and Kricketune fully healed.
I’m inside Julia’s gym. Its puzzle uses Voltorb to remove the metal gates after trainer battles. Marshtomp should reach the level-20 hard cap while clearing these trainers.
The first gate is open. Two Sonic Booms took a large chunk of Marshtomp’s HP, so I’ll restore the team before Julia; the next trainer’s Mareep has no damaging move that can hit Marshtomp.
Three gym trainers are beaten and the first two gates are cleared. I’m saving healing supplies for Julia and will visit the Pokémon Center before the leader battle.
All four gym trainers and gates are cleared, and Marshtomp has reached the level-20 cap. I’m healing now, then going straight to Julia.
Julia’s battle has started. Marshtomp will use Mud Shot against the grounded Electric Pokémon and Water Gun against Oricorio, with healing ready for Sonic Boom damage.
Minun is down, and Marshtomp still has 54/60 HP. Julia is sending in Oricorio, so I’m switching attacks to Water Gun.
Oricorio is down. Its boosted Air Cutter required the Super Potion; Marshtomp has 22 HP left. Electrode is next, so I’m managing healing around its 20-damage Sonic Boom.
Electrode knocked out Kricketune. I’m using the remaining Potion to give Marshtomp another chance to finish it; the other team members can cover that healing turn.
Electrode is down, but Marshtomp is hanging on at 2 HP. I’ll finish this attempt; if Julia’s remaining Pokémon stop us, I’ll adjust the team and supplies before retrying.

That attempt ended in a loss. Marshtomp handled Julia’s Electric attacks, but Oricorio and Sonic Boom exhausted our healing. I’m training Kricketune to the level cap and restocking before the rematch.
I’m back at the Grand Hall, where repeatable trainers award experience candy and heal the party after each win. That should bring Kricketune up to level 20 quickly and earn money for supplies.
The training battles are straightforward: Marshtomp knocks out Emile’s Nidoran in one Mud Shot. I’m using the candy rewards on Kricketune so it can contribute more in the rematch.
Kricketune is now level 20 and has learned Sing in place of Bide. I’m buying healing items, then heading back to Julia.
I’ve restocked with 10 Potions. For the rematch, I’m leading with level-20 Technician Kricketune to build Fury Cutter’s power, with a fully healthy Marshtomp ready to switch in.
Kricketune knocked out Minun in one Fury Cutter without taking damage. Julia chose Alolan Geodude next; I’m switching to Marshtomp, which is immune to its Electric-type Self-Destruct.
Geodude is down, and Marshtomp entered the Oricorio matchup at full health. Kricketune is still untouched, which gives us a much stronger backup for Electrode and Voltorb this time.
Rattata covered one healing turn, and Bidoof survived the next because Electrode missed. Marshtomp is restored for the fight, while Kricketune remains healthy for Julia’s last two Pokémon.
Electrode is down, and Marshtomp still has 40 HP. Only Voltorb and Plusle remain; Kricketune is going in at full health.
Julia is defeated! Kricketune finished both Voltorb and Plusle with Fury Cutter. I’m collecting the badge rewards, saving here, and finalizing the recording before stopping.
The save now confirms the Volt Badge, and the game is paused inside Julia’s room. The final recording has finished exporting; I’m checking the video and saving the continuation notes.

Julia defeated—Volt Badge and TM57 Charge Beam obtained. Saved and stopped inside her gym as requested.

- **Trainer:** Aster, separate save `Game_3`, HARDCAP only.
- **Main team:** Marshtomp 20 and Technician Kricketune 20.
- **Archive:** Four idle-trimmed, 4× videos totaling 25m45s and 64 MB.

[Recordings and checkpoint details](/Users/jw/Documents/ChatGPT/Reborn/README.md) · [Run notes](/Users/jw/Documents/ChatGPT/Reborn/notes/run.md)
I’ll plan the route and Florinia’s team before continuing, restart the recording, and stop after earning the second badge.

Florinia’s main threats are Cradily’s defensive setup, Breloom’s Spore, and Desert Field-boosted attacks. I’ll prepare level-25 Kricketune with Protective Pads, add a Flying-type option, and stock up on the slums’ cheaper Fresh Water. I’ve also reviewed Cain, the Scraggy gang, PULSE Tangrowth, and Fern along the route.
The recording is running, and Victoria has opened the route toward Obsidia. I’m healing first, then I’ll strengthen the team before entering the slums.
The route plan is saved, including each major opponent and the items to collect. The first stop is Grand Hall training; after Julia, its rewards increase to four experience candies per win.
Kricketune beat Servine and reached level 21. Marshtomp is handling Quilava. I’m keeping the type matchups planned rather than letting the battle script run through every opponent with one attack.

I caught an input-script issue: OCR occasionally misses the move-menu PP label, which caused one unintended Absorb. I’m fixing that recognition before repeating training battles. The game state and saves remain unmodified.
The first training win is complete, and the party has been healed automatically. I’ll put these four candies into Marshtomp so the remaining training battles are quicker and safer.
Marshtomp is now level 24, and Kricketune has reached 23. I’m using Mud Shot against Quilava as well as Nidorino—it hits both super effectively and is stronger than Water Gun.

The stronger Marshtomp took only two Mud Shots to beat Quilava. I’ve also added an Emile-specific routine that switches between our two main Pokémon at the planned matchups, while still stopping for move learning or uncertain screens.
Both main Pokémon are now at the level-25 cap and fully healed. I’m moving on to Obsidia, where I’ll add Flying coverage before the slums and PULSE Tangrowth.
The team is ready for the route. I’m clearing the bridge trainer on the way to Victoria’s checkpoint, then heading into Obsidia’s railnet to look for Woobat.

Obsidia’s checkpoint is open. I’m locating the railnet entrance and collecting useful route information before heading south; Kricketune and Marshtomp are both capped, so the next training investment will go into a new teammate.

Franklin’s Togedemaru is cleared. One useful detail from the walkthrough: the slums contain a free Friend Ball. I’ll use that for Woobat so its friendship evolution is practical, and catch a slums Pokémon for immediate backup along the way.
The team is at the current level cap. I’m working through the slums route next, collecting the Friend Ball and supplies before preparing our Grass-gym counters.
Davinson is cleared. I’m checking the slums entrances against the installed map: this area has several exits that lead to different floors, so the route needs the correct starting doorway.
The correct entrance is on the south side; the upper doors are exits from later floors. The nearby Flying trainer is next, so Marshtomp will handle that battle.
Wayne’s accuracy-lowering moves have stretched this battle out. I’m healing Marshtomp and checking the move selection before finishing his last Pokémon.
Wayne is defeated, but Marshtomp fainted after repeated misses. I’m restoring the team before entering the slums; the next trainer has a Fire type, so going in depleted would waste supplies.
The party is fully healed. I’m pausing here for the hourly recording export, trimming the idle gaps and saving this segment at 4× speed before resuming.

The export is verified: about 56 minutes of capture became a five-minute archive after idle removal and 4× playback. macOS changed the capture-device numbering, so I’m reconnecting the recorder while the game remains paused.
Recording has resumed and the return route is clear. In the slums I’ll preserve the healing shards until needed and pick up the free supplies before the Victoria fight.
The entrance Potion is collected. I’m tightening the navigation checks around item messages so queued movement only continues after the game has fully returned to the map.
Rafe’s Pansear went down in one Mud Shot. The next stretch is mostly Psychic and Normal opponents, where Kricketune’s Fury Cutter is a good fit; the healing shard comes before Victoria.
Omar is cleared without taking damage. Both main Pokémon remain healthy, so I can save the next healing shard for after the remaining slums trainers.
We reached Victoria with both main Pokémon still at full health. I’ll use Kricketune for her opening Pokémon, then switch to Marshtomp for Torracat.
Victoria’s Ralts and Torracat are down without damage. Marshtomp is handling the remaining pair; afterward the route opens into the basement encounters and supply rooms.
Victoria is defeated, including her optional relationship-point battle. I’ll use the nearby shard now to restore Marshtomp and replenish moves before searching the basement.
The basement supply detour is underway. The Carbos here can fund healing items, and I’m watching the encounters for a Flying-type backup while continuing toward the roof and elevator shortcut.
Caught a level-13 Pidove. Once it learns Air Cutter and evolves, it will give us a useful Grass- and Fighting-type counter alongside the planned Woobat.
The Carbos is collected, and the team now includes Pidove. I’m heading through the upper slums toward Corey and the elevator, which opens the shortcut to the Friend Ball and the Scraggy gang.
Marshtomp is facing Joltik to avoid Thunder Wave and Electroweb. The next section has scripted jumps across broken flooring, so I’m mapping those transitions before queuing the route.
The broken-floor section is crossed. Next are the upper-floor items and rooftop healing shard, then the elevator shortcut into the gang’s basement.
I’ve added the floor-jump transitions to the route helper. It can now cross these gaps with ordinary key presses and pause for encounters, which should make this section much smoother.
Corey’s scene is complete and the Zinc is collected. I’m taking the nearby Exp. Candy as well, then returning to the rooftop route.

The route helper exposed one input issue: very brief direction taps occasionally failed to turn toward an item. I’ve changed item interactions to use the reliable held-key timing and am verifying pickups before moving on.
The upper-floor supplies are secured, including the Moon Stone. I’m following the loop to the roof now; the next trainer’s Paras will get non-contact attacks to avoid Effect Spore.
Mason is cleared without taking damage or status. I’m healing at the rooftop shard before the gang sequence, which will also wake up the newly caught Pidove.
The first-floor elevator shortcut is open. I’m descending to buy Fresh Water and collect the Friend Ball before the Scraggy gang battle.
Fresh Water is stocked. I’m at the side passage for the Friend Ball; after this, the remaining basement route leads to the gang battle and Coral Ward.
The Friend Ball is secured. This is a good stopping point for the next hourly archive: I’m saving and pausing here, exporting the recording, then resuming toward Coral Ward.
The second export is verified: 5 minutes 23 seconds, about 9 MB. Recording has restarted, and I’m resuming from the Friend Ball room.
The second shortcut is open and the Net Ball is collected. I’m taking the brief elevator detour for TM60, then entering the gang’s rooms.
TM60 is collected. I’m returning to B1F for Dax and the Scraggy gang; Kricketune and Marshtomp will lead the double battle, with healing ready if needed.
Dax’s team is being cleared cleanly. The gang battle is next; I’ll concentrate attacks to remove one opponent at a time and prioritize Scrafty when it enters.
The first Scraggy is down. Swagger caused Kricketune to hurt itself, so I’m using Fresh Water while Marshtomp finishes the weakened opponent.

Swagger overwhelmed the two-Pokémon core, and Pidove is still too low-level to cover it. I’m reloading the pre-battle save and finishing the Flying-type training before another attempt; we’ll need those counters for the park and Gym #2 as well.
The reload preserved all collected items and shortcuts. I’m using those shortcuts to return for Woobat and training, so the next attempt will have a full set of usable counters.
I’m preparing two Flying-type counters before returning to the Scraggy gang. They’ll also cover the park’s Tangrowth and Florinia’s Grass team, so this training serves the rest of the route.
The route back is clear. I’m saving the Friend Ball for Woobat: its friendship boost will make Swoobat available sooner, giving us a fast special attacker alongside Tranquill.

I’m checking the Railnet encounter area while keeping the party ready to catch Woobat. Once it’s secured, I’ll use the Grand Hall’s repeatable candy rewards to bring both new team members to the level cap.
The first encounter was Klink. I’ve switched the faster Kricketune back into the lead so we can escape unwanted encounters reliably, then bring Pidove in to weaken Woobat.
Turbo made the short movement loop cross the Railnet exit. I’ve stopped the loop and am restoring the movement speed used by the mapped routes before continuing the encounter search.
Woobat has appeared at level 13. I’m weakening and putting it to sleep before using the Friend Ball; that should give us a dependable catch without risking the only one we have.
Woobat is now in catching range of the team’s weaker moves. After this catch I’ll rotate the recording archive, then proceed with the planned training.
The cave weakens Gust, so Pidove’s chip damage is too small here. Marshtomp can use Tackle to lower Woobat’s health more effectively; I’m keeping its stronger moves out of this catch.
Woobat is caught in the Friend Ball. I’m saving this progress and processing the current recording before starting the training segment.
The seventh archive is verified: about 4½ minutes at 4× speed, with idle gaps removed. Woobat has Unaware, which is useful against stat boosts; the next recording is running.
I’m returning to the Grand Hall to heal and train. The priority is reaching the Flying evolutions and Air Cutter before the Slums rematch, then topping off levels before Florinia.
The catch is safely saved, and we’re back at the Grand Hall. I’ll heal the team, then use the established Kricketune/Marshtomp matchups for the repeat battles.

The first training battle is following the expected pattern: Kricketune handles Servine, then Marshtomp switches in for Quilava. Turbo is enabled only for these battles, keeping the navigation timing consistent.
The training matchup is stable so far, with Kricketune staying healthy and Marshtomp handling the Fire and Poison opponents. Each win supplies four Exp. Candies and a full heal.
Woobat’s Friend Ball starts it at 200 friendship, and Swoobat needs 220. Level gains and walking should cover that threshold during this training, saving the salon expense.
Two rematches are complete. Two more will provide enough candy for both Flying evolutions and Air Cutter, after which I’ll return to the story route with four usable battlers.

For the gang rematch, both Flying types can use Air Cutter to hit both opponents at once. That avoids Intimidate’s Attack reduction and should clear the smaller Scraggy before they stack Swagger and Sand Attack.
The third rematch needed one extra hit on Quilava. Marshtomp still has enough health to finish the last Nidorino, and the automatic heal will reset the team afterward.
This is the last preparation rematch before returning to the Slums. I’ll give Pidove seven candies and Woobat eleven, retain their useful attacking moves, and verify both evolutions before leaving.
The four wins supplied all 18 candies, and everyone is healed. I’m applying them now and replacing the birds’ weaker utility moves with Air Cutter and recovery where available.
Pidove has learned Air Cutter and is now learning Roost. I’m keeping Quick Attack for priority and replacing the less useful status moves.
Tranquill is evolved at level 21. Woobat’s candy gains should also carry it past the friendship threshold; I’m finishing its move choices, including Air Cutter.
Both evolutions are complete: Tranquill and Swoobat are ready. I’m verifying their moves and saving, then heading back through the opened elevator shortcut for the gang rematch.
The saved team now has Swoobat level 22 and Tranquill level 21, both with Air Cutter. Their speed and spread damage give us a much stronger answer to the Slums double battle.

I found why the movement speed changed: Reborn automatically restores normal overworld speed after a battle. I’ve corrected the control routine so it won’t toggle turbo a second time when the battle ends.
We’re back on the route to the Slums. The elevator shortcuts let us bypass the earlier maze; the remaining sequence is the gang, Coral Ward, the park, and the Onyx school before Florinia.
The team is back inside the Slums. I’m setting the two Flying types in the opening slots before entering the gang room, with Kricketune and Marshtomp held in reserve.
We’ve reached the gang-room approach. I’ll save immediately outside the trigger and check each double-battle turn rather than queueing past a knockout or switch.
The rematch is underway with both Flying types healthy. Air Cutter targets both Scraggy, so there’s no single-target selection to slow the opening down.
All three Scraggy are down. Scrafty hit Swoobat hard with Payback, but it’s already below half health and both of our Flying types move first.
The gang is defeated with no knockouts or items used. I’m saving the win and healing Swoobat before moving on to Coral Ward.
The battle is won, but Scrafty’s exit animation appears to be stuck at the gate. I’m checking the event sequence before taking any recovery action so we don’t lose the win unnecessarily.
The exit sequence has completed and normal controls are back. No reset was needed; I’m saving through the menu and continuing.
The win is confirmed in the save. I’m using the remaining light shard for a free full heal, then taking the newly opened passage onward.
The light shard restored the whole team. I’m collecting the useful healing items along the exit route before the next rival battle.
The gang’s passage is open. I’m taking the nearby Potion and Exp. Candy, then heading toward the basement exit and Coral Ward.
The exit area has several useful supplies, including a Cotton Candy revive. I’m collecting these now so the park and school battles won’t depend on our small cash reserve.
The new team and the free healing supplies are in place. After Coral, I’ll focus on the park’s one-time pickups and the school’s Protective Pads before challenging Florinia.
The supplies now include a revive, a Super Potion, status cures, and another candy. I’m finishing this short side passage and then leaving the Slums.
A wild Pancham interrupted the pickup route. I’m clearing that encounter, then resuming the exit path.
The extra supplies are collected. I’m retracing the two short passages to the escalator, then opening the final shortcut through the Slums.
Swoobat is handling the incidental wild encounters cleanly. I’m continuing to the escalator; the next recording rotation is approaching, so I’ll pause at the next safe checkpoint.
One more wild encounter interrupted the escalator approach. The exit trigger requires approaching from its left side; I’ve checked that and am adjusting the route.
We’re through the basement and back on the upper floor. I’m opening the backpacker’s shortcut, then pausing to archive this hour of play before the Coral section.
The shortcut is open and the game is saved and paused. I’m exporting session eight with idle gaps removed at 4× speed; the next segment will start with the final Slums pickups and Coral Ward.
Session eight is verified: 7 minutes 23 seconds at 4× speed. Recording has restarted, and I’m continuing from the saved shortcut.
The game isn’t responding to the usual key holds after the recording restart. I’m checking the app’s focus and capture state before sending more movement commands.

The controls are responding again, but the capture check revealed that macOS reassigned the recording-device numbers and selected a camera. I’m stopping that capture and switching back to the screen before continuing; the brief pickup segment wasn’t recorded correctly.
The screen capture is now verified. I’ve switched it to the device’s name rather than its changing number, and removed the incorrect camera footage. Continuing toward Coral now.
The Awakening is collected for Florinia’s Spore, and I’ve reached the final Slums corridor. I’m starting the nearby Spoink encounter for later, then exiting to Coral.
We’ve reached Coral Ward. Cain’s team is planned for: Marshtomp handles his Alolan Grimer and Cubone, while Kricketune covers Popplio; the Flying types remain available as backups.
I’ve located Coral’s Pokémon Center. I’ll heal there, put Marshtomp in front for Cain’s opening Grimer, and then trigger the dock scene.
The party is healed and reordered for Cain. Marshtomp and Kricketune are the first two slots, with both Flying types healthy behind them.

The dock rescue scene is underway. The party screen kept its cursor on the swapped slot, so the reorder left Kricketune leading; I’ve verified the actual order and will select Marshtomp explicitly when the battle begins.
Cain’s battle has started. I’m bringing Marshtomp into the confirmed sixth slot for the opening matchup.
Grimer is down, and Cain is sending Popplio next. I’m switching to Kricketune so the mist-boosted Icy Wind won’t hit one of our Flying types.
Popplio is down. Kricketune’s Fury Cutter is now powered up, so I’m keeping that chain for Cubone while watching its health for the final Nidorino.
Cain is down to a weakened Nidorino. Kricketune still has enough health to finish it with the next Fury Cutter, with Marshtomp healthy in reserve.
Cain is defeated, and the dock scene is finished. I’m checking the Cut reward, then returning to Obsidia Park.
Cut is confirmed in the bag. I’m healing once more before the park, where the Forest Field changes move strength and makes Tangrowth’s healing the main threat.
I’m teaching Cut to our utility Pokémon. I also noticed Swoobat can learn Charge Beam from the TM we already have, giving it a useful way to raise Special Attack before tougher fights.
